_what_this_is: A PROPOSAL. Nothing here has been written to any registry. Produced by re-measuring the 37 artifacts named in doc/reports/root_scale.md with the fixed commons/testing/measure_artifacts.gd, four independent headless Godot runs, and joining the result against tools/sync_footprints.py's footprint formula, tools/spatial_contract.py's resolution order and tools/slot_capacity.py's authored museum slots. A human must review before any of it lands.

method.stability_rule_as_briefed: two readings, discard if they disagree by > 1%
method.stability_rule_used: four readings, discard if any axis' full range exceeds one 0.01 m snap step. The briefed 1% rule has a RESOLUTION FLOOR: aabb_size is snapped to 0.01 m, so on any axis under 1.00 m a single snap step already exceeds 1%. Applied literally to two runs it discarded VectorBasics (0.74/0.73), VectorCrossProduct (0.72/0.73) and VectorForces (0.80/0.81), all of which are stable to the centimetre across four runs — and it CERTIFIED vector_arena, constraints and spherecolors, which are not.
method.slot_capacity: recomputed IN MEMORY at max_probe=22 by importing tools/slot_capacity.py and calling analyse() directly, so no file was written and the shipped probe ceiling of 8 does not truncate large bodies. commons/data/slot_capacity.json is byte-identical to HEAD.
method.slot_fit_test: footprint [w,d] fits a slot if some cardinal rotation's max_w x max_d contains it; at 90/270 the pair is swapped. This is containment only — it does not re-run clearance or access negotiation.

prediction_written_before_measuring.question: how many of the 37 have footprint_cells actually change
prediction_written_before_measuring.verdict: off by one. The miss is vector_arena: predicted to move 6 -> 2 cells, it came back UNSTABLE — bit-identical in runs 1, 2 and 3 and then 1.48 -> 1.65 m on the Y axis in run 4. Two readings would have certified it and the prediction would have scored. The prediction was wrong for the right reason and the rule caught it.

headline.why: It is the most-placed of the 37 by a factor of two (43 map cells in 43 maps), its body grows 1.5x on every axis from 4.75 x 3.35 x 3.35 to 7.13 x 5.02 x 5.02, its oriented footprint goes 5x4 -> 8x6 cells (20 -> 48 raw), and the authored museum slots that can hold it collapse from 71 to 7 of 475. And its scalar spatial_needs.footprint_cells does NOT move: 9 -> 9, because both sides are above the cap. sync_footprints.py would report nothing at all for this artifact, so the correction that most changes placement is the one invisible to the tool meant to propagate it. It is also perfectly stable — [7.13, 5.02, 5.02] to the byte in all four runs.
headline.runner_up_why: The largest single slot swing: 3.2x on every axis, 1.32^3 -> 4.22^3, footprint_cells 4 -> 9 (raw 4 -> 25), slots 328 -> 32 of 475. Its own source corroborates the number twice: pickable_xyz.gd:27 declares initial_scale = Vector3(3.2, 3.2, 3.2) with a critical_parameter note that 3.2x is what makes the labels readable in VR, and line 226 describes the body as '1.2 m rods times the 3.2x initial_scale'. 1.32 x 3.2 = 4.224.

caveats: The 1% rule's resolution floor (see method.stability_rule_used) is the single most consequential detail here. Two readings are not enough: vector_arena was bit-identical three times and then moved 10.3%.

The script's own stability check fired on six artifacts, and it is neither sound nor complete against cross-run reproducibility. It flagged numerical_integration, which is bit-identical across all four runs (running, but deterministically), and it did NOT flag spherecolors or vector_arena, which are not reproducible. Within-run growth and between-run agreement are different questions and the script only asks the first.
three_body_problem is a runaway simulation, not a body: 147-157 m wide across four runs. Its number is meaningless at any scale and its shipped footprint_cells of 1 is wrong for that separate reason.

cloth_simulation and fluid_simulation each appear in TWO registry files (physics_simulation.json + soft_bodies.json, physics_simulation.json + algorithms_misc.json). measure_artifacts.gd keys by lookup_name and the later file wins, so a sync must decide which copy it is writing.

None of the 37 has a hand-authored entry in commons/artifacts/artifact_spatial_contracts.json, so measurements.grid_cells is authoritative for every one of them in tools/spatial_contract.py. There is no hand value shielding any of these from the change.

Slot acceptance is footprint containment against the authored slot table. It is an indicator of placement pressure, not a placement run. 36 of the 475 slots are still probe-clipped at 22 cells, so counts for very large bodies are lower bounds.
vector_arena's shipped footprint_source is 'estimated', the only one of the 37 that is not 'measured'.

The nine unstable artifacts split by cause, which decides the remedy. UNSEEDED RNG (a seed export plus a dna.fixture would fix them): bouncing_ball, collision_detection, force_fields, spherecolors — all four call randf/randi in their build. TIME-DOMAIN ANIMATION (needs a pinned phase, not a seed): three_body_problem, constraints, spring_mass_system, VectorMotion, vector_arena — no RNG at all, they are simply somewhere else when the shutter opens. collision_detection is the worst at 56.99% across four runs; it is not measurable at all in its present form.

A concurrent session was writing registry files throughout this run (commons/artifacts/registry/*.json, mtimes 04:28-04:40). The baseline was re-read afterwards and none of the 37 entries moved. The primary before/after pair does not depend on the registry in any case: old_aabb.same_run_root_local_size is computed inside the same instantiation as the new number, so the count of 17 is immune to concurrent writes. Only the shipped_footprint_cells column reads the registry.
